probes.title: repeat-decode stability (PASS) and cross-reader-lane digest dependence (MEASURED FACT)
probes.note: MATERIAL FINDING, not a stability failure. Repeat decode is bit-identical. But the physical-metadata digest is ALSO reader-lane dependent: the encoding and authority_status fields of reader_configuration are inside the digest payload. A frozen digest is therefore valid only for its exact reader lane. O1-C05/O1-C06 must bind the reader lane together with the source identity.

residuals_explicitly_not_claimed_as_pass.subject: pandas.Timestamp is outside the D02 opaque carrier
residuals_explicitly_not_claimed_as_pass.statement: The accepted D02 contract uses EXACT type identity (type(value) in {datetime,date,time}). pandas.Timestamp subclasses datetime.datetime, so a Timestamp is NOT captured and falls through _physical_value to _jsonable, which collapses it to a string.
residuals_explicitly_not_claimed_as_pass.measured: Naive Timestamp -> '2008-04-05 06:07:08'; tz-aware Timestamp -> a DIFFERENT string. Probe D02-3 confirms the two renderings differ, so tz-awareness changes identity on that lane.
residuals_explicitly_not_claimed_as_pass.consequence: This is a property of the ACCEPTED decoder as merged. It is not a defect introduced by this qualification and is NOT repaired here. It is recorded because it bounds exactly what the D02 date@1 carrier does and does not cover.
